answer: Each agent must pass through a registry inlet that mints a one-time hardware attestation token. This token acts as a pigment — once bound to an identity thread, it cannot be washed and reapplied, because the attestation references a physical TPM seed burned at manufacture. The timestamped moment of trust transfer is the registry's on-chain confirmation of that token hash. A second registration attempt produces a hash collision, so the transfer is provably non-repeatable.
